claim: G33 R12 R3: a no-inference package correction can close the four already-passing R2 developmental re-expression claims while explicitly hash-preserving every pre-existing user-owned G22/G28 worktree path omitted by the R2 plan.
non_claims: No new model call, candidate, trial, consequence, runtime behavior, code change, evidence reinterpretation, clean initial daemon exit, general cognition, production promotion, final G33, or whole-PoC acceptance.
rationale: R2 passed its runtime and independent verifier, but its closure package failed because the frozen plan omitted existing user-owned G22/G28 paths from preserved classification. The fidelity checker must not be weakened and the user's work must not be staged or modified. R3 changes only the plan boundary: it pins the completed R2 implementation/evidence and every omitted user path, then reruns offline identity and semantic review with zero inference or effects.
reading: Read both controls; BUILD_FIDELITY_PROTOCOL; R2 frozen plan, attempt ledger, outcome, semantic audit, passing verifier, freeze, observations, verdict, exact provider claim/response, trial/ranking/restart/severance evidence; R2 closure-check failure; and the exact current hashes of every pre-existing unstaged G22/G28 path.
representation: Make no runtime or evidence change. Represent the omitted worktree baseline as explicit preserved entries. Rerun the independent R2 verifier and actual-secret absence check offline, record their bounded result under R3 docs, and construct a closure whose limitations retain the initial SIGTERM/large-projection fact.
consumer: The builder-side fidelity checker consumes the R3 plan, preserved hashes, R2 evidence hashes, four qualified claim results, and semantic review. No Miter cognitive consumer, model, Keychain disclosure, live service, or effect membrane is invoked except read-only actual-secret comparison for evidence hygiene.
falsifiers: Any preserved user path or R2 source/evidence hash changes; any user path is staged; any runtime/code/config/evidence mutation occurs; a provider claim or request is added; the independent verifier or actual-secret scan fails; the initial SIGTERM is relabelled clean; a bounded claim is broadened; or the fidelity closer still reports an unclassified path.
scope_review: R3 may add only docs/gates/G33/R12/R3. It may read committed R2 evidence and user-owned preserved files and run offline hash/verifier/secret-absence checks. It may not edit source, config, fixtures, scripts, evidence, controls, prior docs, user G22/G28 work, credentials, services, or Git history.
rollback: Remove only the new R3 documentation if the package correction fails; retain R1/R2 implementation, all evidence, both call claims, and every user-owned path exactly. No external state changes.

cases.positive: All preserved hashes match; the independent R2 verifier and actual-secret absence audit pass; the closure checker accepts exactly four bounded claims.
cases.severed: Changing any R2 evidence/source or omitted user path, adding a provider claim, or removing the disclosed initial-process limit prevents closure.
cases.neutral: The package correction changes no runtime meaning and adds no evidence-derived standing.
cases.restored: Restoring exact preserved bytes restores package validity without inference or effects.
cases.held_out: No new runtime held-out case; R3 is a package-boundary correction only.
cases.unknown_malformed: Missing, altered, unclassified, or staged user files and failed verifier/secret checks remain explicit closure failures.

environment: Offline builder-side fidelity validation over committed R2 evidence; zero model calls, network requests, live services, runtime mutations, credentials emitted, or external effects.
next_step_hypothesis: If R3 closes, separately derive the next G33 plan for compact hash-bound proof projections and the final clean-start integration/report. If it fails, preserve the first package discrepancy and change no runtime.
